title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Term 3. Term 4 is set aside for revision and the final examinations.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Analytical Geometry: Circles and Tangents

questions.prompt: The centre of $(x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 9$ is…
What is the radius of $x^2 + y^2 = 49$?
Find the radius of $x^2 + y^2 + 4x - 2y - 4 = 0$.
The point $(3; 4)$ lies on the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 25$.
Where does the point $(1; 1)$ lie relative to $x^2 + y^2 = 4$?
Find the equation of the circle with centre $(-1; 2)$ passing through $(2; 6)$.
Find the equation of the tangent to $x^2 + y^2 = 20$ at the point $(2; 4)$.
A(−2; 1) and B(4; 9) are the endpoints of a diameter. Find the equation of the circle.

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Euclidean Geometry: Proportionality and Similarity

questions.prompt: Two triangles are similar if they are…
△ABC ||| △DEF with AB = 6, DE = 9 and BC = 8. Find EF.
If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
In right-angled △ABC with $\hat{A} = 90^\circ$, AD ⊥ BC, BD = 4 and DC = 9. Find AD.
In △ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with AD = 3, DB = 6, AE = 4 and EC = 8. Prove that DE ∥ BC.
questions.memo:
✓ $\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ (1)
✓ $\frac{AE}{EC} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$ (1)
✓ $\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC}$ (1)
✓ DE ∥ BC (line divides two sides of △ in prop) (1)

questions.prompt: In △ABC, D lies on BC with BD : DC = 2 : 3. Find the ratio area △ABD : area △ADC and give a reason.
questions.memo:
✓ The triangles have the same height from A (1)
✓ so their areas are in the ratio of their bases (1)
✓ $2 : 3$ (1)

questions.prompt: In a scatter plot the points fall from left to right. The correlation is…
Which value cannot be a correlation coefficient?
The regression line is $\hat{y} = 12 + 3{,}5x$. Predict $y$ when $x = 8$.
The least-squares regression line always passes through $(\bar{x}; \bar{y})$.
Why is it risky to use a regression line to make predictions far outside the range of the data?
questions.memo:
✓ The relationship may not continue in the same way beyond the data (1)
✓ so predictions may be unrealistic or impossible (1)

questions.prompt: A study finds a strong positive correlation between shoe size and reading ability in primary school children. Does a bigger foot cause better reading? Explain.
questions.memo:
✓ No (1)
✓ Both increase with age (a third variable); correlation does not prove causation (1)

questions.prompt: What does a correlation coefficient of $r = 0{,}2$ tell you about predictions made with the regression line?
questions.memo:
✓ The linear correlation is weak (1)
✓ so predictions will not be reliable (1)

questions.prompt: A learner has 4 shirts, 3 pairs of trousers and 2 pairs of shoes. How many different outfits are possible?
Evaluate $\dfrac{7!}{5!}$.
How many 5-digit codes can be made from the digits 0 to 9 if digits may be repeated?
In how many ways can 5 boys and 3 girls sit in a row if the girls must sit together?
questions.memo:
✓ Treat girls as one unit: $6!$ (1)
✓ Girls among themselves: $3!$ (1)
✓ $720 \times 6 = 4\ 320$ (1)

questions.prompt: A 4-digit code is formed using the digits 1 to 9 without repetition. What is the probability that the code is an even number?
questions.memo:
✓ Total: $9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 3\ 024$ (1)
✓ Last digit even: 4 choices (2, 4, 6, 8) (1)
✓ Even codes: $4 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 1\ 344$ (1)
✓ $P = \frac{1\ 344}{3\ 024} = \frac{4}{9}$ (1)
